import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_72/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_72/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_72_0 and Source3_72_1 on "city"
# Both have a 'city' column, join on that
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by ["Source3_72_0.city", "Source3_72_1.type"], aggregations ["avg(Source3_72_0.fare)"]
# After join, columns are: city, date, fare, ride_id, driver_count, type
# Group by city and type, aggregate avg of fare

result = (
    df_joined
    .groupby(["city", "type"], as_index=False)
    .agg({"fare": "mean"})
)

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
# Target schema: ['city': string, 'type': string, 'fare': float]
result = result.rename(columns={"fare": "fare"})

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_72/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_72/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_72/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city' (inner join by default)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' (primary key) and aggregate average fare
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "type": "first"  # 'type' is functionally dependent on city, so taking first is safe
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[["city", "type", "fare"]]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_72/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
